author: Disappointed Hide.Me User
title: Default App Behavior Ruins Every Video Experience
content: When scrolling to select a video the moment you stop to read a title, or look at the poster frame, the video instantly starts playing.  By default there is no audio.  If you touch the video to watch it advertising will play, which is expected.  Whatâs not expected is that when the opportunity to leave the ads and go to the video appears, the video CONTINUES playing with audio, but 5, 10, or whatever number of seconds in from when you touched it.  This means in order to watch from the beginning the user must use the navigation.  Very annoying since the initial play back is silent and instantaneous before selecting the video for viewing.  After selection, and pre-roll ads the video should start from the BEGINNING.  Beyond that, this whole âinstant playâ thing when scrolling should be a user selectable feature that can be turned on or off.  Personally, I like to read the title and look at the poster frame before making a selection.  Whatâs the point of allowing the content providers to write titles and make custom poster frames if viewers arenât able to see them?  If it were books instead of videos, itâd be like flashing the title and cover and then start instantly into the bookâs text before I even know if Iâm interested.  Also, auto-starting the video may spoil any given viewing experience by revealing something before the viewer is allowed to watch the video as the author intended.  PLEASE remove this behavior or allow the viewer to control it. Thank you.

author: frogman3126
title: Unnecessarily cluttered, non-intuitive, with multiple issues
content:
I am surprised at the percentage of 5-star ratings for this app which I find substandard especially given that the service is owned by Google. It is indeed cluttered and has an unnecessarily steep learning curve, but letâs be a little specific too. Among its (numerous) problems, if one searches for and saves a group of videos already packaged as a playlist â course lectures, say â it will appear as a playlist in your collection but not on the list of playlists accessed from the menu by which a new but related video could be added to it. Such a video, even though it would be most usefully seen in the context of the original collection, must be placed in a new playlist. Do they really need to protect the integrity of the original playlist? More: if a video download is (inadvertently?) deleted, the item stays on the list and is streamable for sure, but any attempt to re-download it fails, even though âDownload againâ is a menu item â and even if recaptured anew through a search and saved, it is recognized as the one previously deleted and will still fail to download. Mind you, I do have the Premium service.
   This is not to mention the sometimes excruciatingly slow download speeds for some videos. This is undoubtedly the consequence of poor bandwidth of the hosting server, not the fault of the app, BUT the app contributes to the problem by not fully supporting downloading when closed â even when it is open in the background, it is significantly slower. This almost forces you to keep the app open and in the foreground for the duration of a long download. A serious waste of my time. Iâll stop here, but only out of psychic fatigue.
